key_insight: A two-stage large language model pipeline can surface many internal inconsistencies in discharge summaries, but reliable detection depends heavily on clinical context and temporal reasoning.
clinical_relevance: Automated inconsistency screening could help flag documentation problems that may affect clinical reasoning, patient safety, and downstream EHR use.
method: Used Gemini 2.5 Pro to identify candidate inconsistencies, then Gemini 2.5 Flash to verify them with context.
Clinicians manually reviewed a subset of outputs to assess failure modes.
evidence_signal: The pipeline produced 3,460 candidate inconsistencies across 69.7% of admissions, with expert review highlighting recurring context-related failure modes.
watch_item: Many flagged issues may reflect missing context rather than true contradictions, so deployment would need careful validation to avoid overcalling inconsistencies.
paper_title: Toward Automated Detection of Documentation Inconsistencies in Electronic Health Records
